summary: Summation No. 25 reports on Occupied Japan for October 1947 (statistics mostly for August-September), under the Katayama coalition Cabinet. Politically it covers the National Public Service Law, the Police Reform Bill following MacArthur's 16 September letter demanding decentralization, the Economic Decentralization Bill, the fight over the 1,800-yen wage standard and the new 1,700-yen rice price, coal control, 51 Imperial princes becoming commoners, and Liberal Party moves toward a new conservative party. Legal chapters give the revised Criminal Code, new judicial laws, war crimes trial totals, and the IMTFE defense cases of Hirota, Itagaki, Kaya, Kido and Kimura. Economic sections track the September typhoon and flood damage, coal, steel, textile, power, rail, labor, trade, rationing, finance, property and reparations figures. Social sections cover nutrition surveys, disease rates, welfare, schools, religion and media. Historians will find detailed production, price and wage data and the full text of SCAP's police-reform letter.
highlights: On 16 September MacArthur replied to Prime Minister Katayama's police plan, demanding full decentralization into local police under civilian commissions, a national rural police and a 125,000-man ceiling; the Cabinet approved a Police Reform Bill of 90 articles on 13 October.

The Diet enacted the National Public Service Law on 16 October, creating a three-member National Personnel Commission to set civil-service standards, with competitive examinations and merit promotion.

On 22 October the Government fixed the 1947 producer rice price at 1,700 yen per koku (up from 550), while insisting on the 1,800-yen monthly wage standard, which labor federations and the press attacked.

Fifty-one Imperial princes and princesses became commoners on 14 October, leaving only the Emperor's immediate family; 47,475,000 yen was approved in retirement allowances, with none for 11 former militarist princes.
The revised Criminal Code, enacted 26 October for effect on 15 November, abolished lese-majeste and wartime treason provisions and the adultery clause discriminating against women.
War crimes figures: 385 suspects tried by 24 October, 368 convicted and 17 acquitted, 33 death sentences (5 executed); 92 more interned in Sugamo, bringing the total to 1,062.

Floods and typhoons of September damaged 572 schools in nine prefectures, cut rail traffic in central Honshu, and caused over 7,000,000,000 yen in farm damage; Bank of Japan notes in circulation reached 167,665,000,000 yen.
On 2 October SCAP designated 17 arsenals holding about 19,054 metalworking machines for advance reparations transfer to China, the Netherlands, the Philippines and the United Kingdom.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover for Summation No. 25 (October 1947), table of contents, and the list of 113 charts, maps and graphs.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Brief digest of the month: no change in SCAP organization, plus short political, economic and social summaries, including the Police Reform Bill, the 1,800-yen wage dispute and the September floods.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: Single paragraph stating there was no change in the organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during October.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Digest of the National Public Service Law (16 Oct), the 1,800-yen wage fight, Police Reform Bill, Economic Decentralization Bill, 51 princes losing status, party maneuvers and the Purge (315 removed centrally).

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Digest of land sales (69,568 cho), flood damage, coal up 188,300 tons, industry output, trade firsts, new rice quotas and price rises, finance (167.7 billion yen notes) and property control.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Digest of nutrition survey, flood sanitation, National Disaster Law (20 Oct), 572 flood-damaged schools, Shosoin airing, SCAP exhibits and press, radio and film developments.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics, public safety, and legal affairs and war crimes, centered on civil-service reform, police decentralization, the Purge, the Criminal Code and the IMTFE defense phase.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Demobilization bureaus ordered transferred or abolished, National Public Service Law, wage and rice-price controversy, party maneuvers, local autonomy bill, Diet extension to 30 November and Purge totals.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Hidden army supplies in Tochigi, 185,229 August offenses, MacArthur's 16 September police letter, gangster drive (about 8,000 arrests), prison population of 82,789 and the Chofu fire destroying 700 houses.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Five judicial laws and the revised Criminal Code, war crimes investigations, apprehensions and trial results (385 tried), and defense presentations at the International Military Tribunal.

sections.title: Japanese Judicial Administration
sections.summary: Diet passed laws on court reserve funds, popular review of Supreme Court judges, judge status and impeachment; Criminal Code abolishes lese-majeste and adultery clauses.

sections.title: Investigation, Apprehension and Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: 1,498 atrocity cases on hand, 31 apprehension orders, 1,062 interned at Sugamo, and 11 trials of 21 persons with sentences up to 20 years.

sections.title: International Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: Court sat throughout October with 11 of 75 accused having finished defenses; evidence and defense statements for Hirota, Itagaki, Kaya, Kido and Kimura.

sections.title: Defense of Koki Hirota
sections.summary: Hirota's defense, heard 26 September-3 October, portrayed the former Foreign Minister and Prime Minister as a liberal diplomat who strove for peace.

sections.title: Defense of Seishiro Itagaki
sections.summary: Defense of the former War Minister and Kwantung Army officer, including cross-examination on whether the China war intensified after he became Minister of War.

sections.title: Defense of Okinori Kaya
sections.summary: Kaya's defense as Finance Minister under Konoye and Tojo and president of the North China Development Company.

sections.title: Defense of Koichi Kido
sections.summary: Defense of the Lord Keeper of the Privy Seal, Koichi Kido, as presented to the Tribunal.

sections.title: Defense of Heitaro Kimura
sections.summary: Kimura, Kwantung Army chief of staff 1940-41 and Vice-minister of War under Tojo, presented his defense on 24-27 October.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Twelve sections on agriculture, mining, industry, textiles, transport, communications, labor, trade, rationing, finance and property, dominated by flood and typhoon effects and power shortages.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Land sales to 312,280 tenants (69,568 cho), 265,979 hectares reclaimed since 1945, flood damage, July milk output of 15,469,000 liters, and marine landings of 113,280 tons.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: September log output fell to 453,320,000 board feet, 6,300,000 acres of forest inaccessible, coal output rose 188,300 tons but missed quota by 17,700, plus oil and mine production.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke 176,900 tons, pig iron falling to 31,063 tons, crude runs 22,557 kiloliters, cement down 13 percent, fertilizer, chemicals, machine tools and rolling stock hampered by power shortages.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: Food processing, brewing, tobacco, pulp and paper, glass, optical and medical instruments, bricks, motor vehicles, leather and farm implements; canned food fell from 848 to 350 tons.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: 905,353 bales of U.S. cotton received, raw silk up 540 bales, rayon exports prioritized for power, wool and cotton output down, plus knit goods, clothing, sundry goods and dyeing.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Registered trucks and buses hit 99,492, rail passengers fell 6.6 percent to 284,246,252 after typhoon damage, electric generation dropped 3.8 percent to 2,368,168,000 kWh, and gas output declined.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: Radiotelegraph service extended to Egypt and about 75 British Commonwealth points on 15 October, 1,090,426 telephones in service, flood repairs, mail, equipment and Ministry finances.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Employment Security Law delayed to 1 December, Economic Reconstruction Council program, communications workers' dispute over the 1,800-yen standard, 762,000-yen labor education plan, wage rises and retrenchment.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: First postwar trade shipments: Korean apples, canned peaches to Singapore, wool via Singapore, tungsten from Korea, buttons to Sweden, with detailed tables by commodity group.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Quotas of 4,582,500 tons of rice and 2,163,750 tons of sweet potatoes, rice price raised to 1,700 yen per koku, imported food 44 percent of rations, new textile coupon system.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: 46 licensed foreign concerns, notes at 167,665,000,000 yen, bank and savings figures, liquidation proceeds, and national debt of 312,091,000,000 yen on 30 September.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: 7,184 reports on neutral and Allied properties, looted property returned to China and the Philippines, precious-metal allocations, 378 cartel applications cleared, and 17 arsenals designated for reparations.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, and education, religion and media of expression, with nutrition and disease statistics, flood school damage and a map of Japan.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: August nutrition survey (Tokyo 1,704 calories), communicable diseases, hospitals, medical supplies worth 609,550,258 yen, narcotics, 3,210,865 persons on public assistance, repatriation and vital statistics.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion and Media of Expression
sections.summary: 572 flood-damaged schools, teacher training, new university standards, Shosoin airing, 81 showings of SCAP exhibits, press, radio, film, SCAP Information Library and a map of Japan.
